label: Wu 2026
setting: four US institutions (setting type not described beyond 'institutions')
diagnosis_mix: macular degeneration 74 (19.2%); glaucoma 65 (16.9%); cataract 25 (6.5%) (primary diagnosis, not mutually exclusive)
recruitment: recruited from four U.S. institutions June 2019-February 2022 to span a broad spectrum of visual function; sampling method (consecutive/convenience) NR in this paper (see original publication ref 7); inclusion: age >=18, VA data available, able to communicate in English; binocular VA -0.3 to 2.0 logMAR (mean 0.58, SD 0.44); fewer normally sighted people than general population (p8)
cohort: same 385 participants as previously published cohort (ref 7; Wu 2024, Screening ID 128)
notes: Secondary analysis; no separate enrolment count (385 'included in this analysis'), n_enrolled set equal to n. VA with habitual correction (Bailey-Lovie, ETDRS or Snellen); binocular VA used, better eye when only monocular available (p2). Diagnoses from physician exam notes and self-report. Items selected post hoc: top 20 of 100 items by AUC, then pairs and triplets (data-driven selection, no external validation). Item performance estimated within the full 100-item survey, may differ if asked alone (p8).
